B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP fee is stated in the official documentation. Access requires an eligible Mixpanel account and organization-level MCP enablement; free plans may be subject to Query API limits.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Free plan; Growth starts at $0 on the pricing page, with paid usage pricing; Enterprise is quote-based.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The pricing page describes event-volume and session-replay usage tiers. It does not specify an MCP-specific charge. MCP requests are limited to 600 per user per hour.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Most organizations require an admin to enable MCP. New free and Growth accounts created after 2026-08-01 have it enabled by default, though admins can disable it. User project roles apply. Experiments and Feature Flags are open beta; Audit Log is limited beta and requires organization admin or owner access. Service Account authentication is beta.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Mixpanel controls service availability and account plans; organization admins control MCP enablement and user/project access; project roles control permissions. The end user controls which account authenticates.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Official hosted documentation lists 64 tools: analytics queries and discovery, dashboards, data management, cohorts, lookup tables, metrics, session replay, experiments, feature flags, and an audit log. Experiment and feature-flag tools are open beta; Get-Audit-Log is limited beta.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool result schema and error formats are not published in the tool list. The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with an invalid_token error during the supplied connection check.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: No resources capability is documented for the product-data MCP server. The separate docs-search MCP is a different endpoint.
No MCP prompts capability is documented for the product-data server.

Official documentation says successful changes made through MCP are written to the Mixpanel audit log with the connected account and Origin MCP. Read-only and failed calls are not logged there. Other request or telemetry logging is not specified.

C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Audit-log entries; exact event schema is documented on a separate MCP Activity page linked from the docs.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The supplied endpoint check returned HTTP 401 and a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge with error invalid_token and resource_metadata https://mcp.mixpanel.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp. Protected-resource metadata: resource https://mcp.mixpanel.com/mcp; authorization server https://auth.mixpanel.com; bearer method header; scopes_supported projects, analysis, events, insights, segmentation, retention, data:read, funnels, flows, data_definitions, alerts, annotations, bookmarks, business_context, cohorts, context, custom_alerts, custom_events, custom_properties, dashboard_reports, experiments, feature_flags, metrics, user_details. Authorization-server metadata: issuer https://auth.mixpanel.com; authorization endpoint https://mixpanel.com/oauth/authorize; token endpoint https://mixpanel.com/oauth/token/; registration endpoint https://mixpanel.com/oauth/mcp/register/; grant types authorization_code and refresh_token; response type code; PKCE S256; token endpoint auth methods none, client_secret_basic, client_secret_post. Docs also describe beta service accounts using a static bearer header. Token lifetime and revocation details were not found.

Your client should automatically re-register and obtain new tokens.", resource_metadata="https://mcp.mixpanel.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"

C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc / Dynamic Client Registration / OAuth authorization code and refresh token grants / PKCE S256 / token endpoint auth methods none, client_secret_basic, client_secret_post. Docs label projects, analysis, events, insights, segmentation, retention, data:read, funnels, flows, data_definitions as mandatory and dashboard_reports, bookmarks, user_details, business_context as optional. D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tools include reads and writes, including destructive dashboard, cohort, and tag deletion. Official tool-list documentation does not publish readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or preview/confirm protocol is documented. Skills recommend audit/review steps, but these are external guidance. 3. OAuth and service accounts are documented. Users inherit existing project roles and access; MCP is organization-enabled, with new free/Growth accounts created after 2026-08-01 enabled by default. Get-Audit-Log requires organization admin or owner. OAuth metadata supports authorization code and refresh token, PKCE S256, and dynamic registration. Token lifetime/revocation and client allowlists are NOT FOUND. 4. US, EU, and India endpoints are documented. No read-only endpoint, tool filter, or write-disable URL mode is documented. Verified Mode flags unverified entities but does not exclude them. 5. Project access follows the authenticated user or service account. Edit-Property supports PII classification; docs do not describe automatic masking or PII exclusion. Docs warn that data is also sent to the selected AI provider and state MCP is not covered by Mixpanel’s BAA. 6. Rate limit: 600 MCP requests/hour/user. Bulk event/property edits are capped at 50 each. Free plans may have Query API access limits. No general result truncation or per-call cost documented. 7. Tool schemas and validation/correction behavior are not published. 8. Successful changes are attributed in the Mixpanel audit log with Origin MCP; read-only and failed calls are excluded. Other telemetry and opt-out are NOT FOUND. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or vendor-reporting action appears in the official list. No MCP upsell-result behavior documented. 10. The server’s initialize instructions are unavailable. The separate public Claude Code plugin supplies skills with agent instructions; these are not server-enforced. 11. No cross-session memory behavior documented. 12. The product endpoint is a flat documented tool list. Separate regional hosts and the separate docs-search MCP exist. No proxying/subservers described. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, or script-execution tool appears in the official tool list.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official list exists at https://docs.mixpanel.com/docs/mcp#available-tools and names 64 tools, including limited-beta Get-Audit-Log. No official total is stated on that page. actions.json contains all 64 official names plus two names only in the Claude connector directory (Get-Event-Details and Get-Property-Names), dated 2026-10; both are marked third-party and unknown availability. Claude’s directory lists 12 tools total, while SourceMedium’s 2026-09 page reports 63 tools (35 read, 28 write) and omits Get-Audit-Log; its names otherwise match the official list. MCP.so had no tool list. Gamut surfaced a partial set, not a stated total. The catalogue differences may reflect an older list.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted server has no public implementation or published initialize/tool schemas from which to serialize context. The public repository is a companion plugin, not the deployed server.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Official docs say MCP Run-Query cannot filter or break down by cohorts, cannot use SCD/profile-history fields, and does not work with Saved Metrics; use the Mixpanel UI for those analyses. Audience targeting and cohort editing are not supported through the MCP tools; use the UI. REST API capabilities are not treated as MCP actions. Sources: https://docs.mixpanel.com/docs/mcp#limitations

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The connector documentation recommends browser OAuth for interactive use and service accounts for headless use. It instructs users to review the AI provider’s data policies and recommends checking applicable privacy compliance. The docs say “use the Mixpanel UI” for unsupported analyses; no tool-level enforcement details are published.
F_documentation.governance_promises: “Users can only see data from projects they already have access to.” “All existing roles and project-level permissions remain in effect.” “Changes an assistant makes through MCP are recorded in the same audit log as changes made in the Mixpanel UI.” Docs also state read-only and failed calls are not logged and note MCP is not covered by the BAA.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Mixpanel describes the hosted server as providing direct access to Mixpanel data and supporting natural-language queries. Organization admins can disable MCP. Documentation states user project permissions remain in effect.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Project permission inheritance, organization enablement, rate limit, audit logging for successful writes, and documented tool limitations are described as product behavior. Their implementation cannot be independently checked because the hosted code and tool schemas are unavailable. Recommendations to review third-party AI-provider policies are user guidance. The server does not document a confirmation mechanism.

contradictions: Protected-resource metadata advertises scopes including alerts, annotations, custom_alerts, custom_events, custom_properties, cohorts, and context that are absent from the official product-data tool list; scopes therefore do not map one-to-one to listed tools. The OAuth authorization-server metadata also omits the `data:read` scope present in protected-resource metadata.
Official docs list 64 tools including Get-Audit-Log, while SourceMedium reports 63 and omits that limited-beta tool.

The Claude connector directory lists Get-Event-Details and Get-Property-Names, which are absent from the current official tool list; they are recorded as third-party additions with unknown availability.
observations_for_research: The endpoint’s resource metadata is available both at the origin and endpoint-path well-known URL; both supplied protected-resource documents name the endpoint-specific resource in the latter and advertise the same scopes.

Official documentation distinguishes open-beta experiment/feature-flag tools from a limited-beta audit-log tool, while the Claude directory publishes a smaller list that does not include the newest official set.
Successful writes are auditable as MCP-origin activity, while read-only and failed calls are expressly excluded from that audit stream.
